title: The science of a good night's sleep
summary_es: Lo que la ciencia dice sobre dormir poco. Nombres en plural, adjetivos negativos, adverbios y un verbo.
text: Scientists have long known that sleep is essential for good health, but recent {{1}} have shown just how much damage a lack of it can do. People who regularly sleep fewer than six hours a night run a much greater risk of heart disease and {{2}}. Their powers of {{3}} suffer too, which makes accidents more likely. {{4}}, many of us still treat sleep as a luxury. We stay up late answering emails and then find it almost {{5}} to get up in the morning. Experts recommend a few simple changes. Keeping the bedroom cool and dark makes a {{6}} difference, and the {{7}} of going to bed at the same time every night is often underestimated. Above all, they say, we should stop feeling guilty about resting: sleep does not make us lazy, it {{8}} us to do everything else better.

gaps.explanation_es: Hace falta un nombre en plural porque el verbo es «have shown». Discover → discovery → discoveries (la y cambia a ies).
Nombre de enfermedad, coordinado con «heart disease». Verbo + -ion.
Colocación: «powers of concentration» = capacidad de concentración. Tras «of» va un nombre.
Adverbio de frase al principio, seguido de coma: surprise → surprising → surprisingly.
El sentido es negativo (no logramos levantarnos): prefijo im- delante de p.
Entre el artículo y el nombre «difference» va un adjetivo: a significant difference.
Tras «the» y antes de «of» va un nombre: important → importance.
Hace falta un verbo en tercera persona (sujeto «it»): prefijo en- para formar el verbo, y -s. «Enable someone to do something» = permitir.
